claims.text: A hybrid MLIP, on-the-fly ab initio correction, and quasi-harmonic workflow can accurately calculate the free-energy surfaces of both solid and fluid phases near melting.
The workflow can retain vibrational entropy, anharmonicity, and electron–vibration coupling.
Using MLIPs will substantially reduce computational cost relative to full ab initio molecular dynamics.
The proposed workflow will outperform TOR-TILD for multicomponent high-entropy systems.
The intended temperature domain is approximately 0.8T_m to 1.2T_m.
The intended material domain includes elemental systems, binaries, and ternary, quaternary, or higher-order high-entropy alloys.
Full ab initio molecular dynamics is to be replaced by an MLIP-based quasi-harmonic free-energy calculation with selective on-the-fly ab initio corrections.
A sparse, representative ab initio training set can capture the essential vibrational and anharmonic physics required by the MLIP.
Interatomic-potential simulations can reproduce selected first-principles and experimental properties of multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
Selective ab initio evaluations will identify and correct regions where the MLIP underperforms.
On-the-fly corrections will ensure accurate modeling of critical entropy contributions.
Combining fast ML evaluations with selective ab initio calculations provides both ML-level speed and ab initio-level precision.
Fusion free energies will agree with full ab initio molecular dynamics within approximately 5 meV/atom.
Predicted melting temperatures will agree with full ab initio molecular dynamics within approximately 50 K.
The workflow will reduce computational time by up to 90% relative to full ab initio molecular dynamics.
The workflow will be two to three times faster than TOR-TILD for multicomponent high-entropy systems.
Applicability has been validated or confirmed from elemental and binary systems through multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
Performance outside the 0.8T_m to 1.2T_m range and in far-from-equilibrium states remains untested.
The ability to capture extreme anharmonic and electron–vibration interactions in the most compositionally complex alloys is not established.
The hypothesis is falsified if any benchmark exceeds a 5 meV/atom phase-free-energy error or a 50 K melting-temperature error relative to explicit ab initio molecular dynamics.

contradictions.description: The boundary states that applicability is already validated or confirmed from elemental systems through multicomponent HEAs, whereas the uncertainty says fidelity in complex alloys is not established and the proposed experiment is still intended to perform that validation.
